findings.text: Subtable processor record holds an identifier, a primary entry callback, a second callback variant accepting an extra argument, an opaque caller context, and a tally of processed entries.
Firmware table header is a union offering two views of shared storage: a generic ACPI table header view and a CDAT table header view.
Subtable header union offers a common header view plus specialized views for HMAT structures, PRMT module headers, CEDT headers and CDAT headers.

Two build variants control library export and init annotation for firmware-table code: one aliases the ACPI library export and init annotation, the other uses a CXL namespaced GPL export with an empty init annotation.
DMA attribute enumeration defines three ordered states: not supported, then non-coherent, then coherent, in increasing capability order.
Firmware-node flag bit indices are consecutive integers zero through five for links-added, not-device, initialized, needs-child-bound-on-add, best-effort and visited.
Firmware-node handle links to a secondary handle, references an operations table, optionally binds a device, anchors supplier and consumer lists reserved for device links, and carries a flags word.
Firmware link flags use bit zero to mark a dependency cycle and bit one to mark a link to be ignored.
Firmware link record pairs supplier and consumer handles, provides a list hook for each side, and stores a small flags field.
Endpoint descriptor carries a port number, an endpoint identifier, and a pointer to the local firmware-node handle.
Software-node graph port and endpoint names follow indexed patterns with an unsigned position, and reference argument vectors are bounded at sixteen 64-bit slots.
Reference arguments structure holds a target firmware-node pointer, a count of valid entries, and a fixed array of sixteen 64-bit argument values.

Firmware-node operations form an optional-method dispatch table covering lifetime handling, device availability and matching, DMA support, property presence and reads, naming, parent and child traversal, reference resolution, graph endpoint navigation, register mapping, interrupt lookup and device-link creation.

Dispatch validates that the handle is usable and that the table and requested method exist. Integer callers distinguish a bad handle from a missing method via different errors, boolean callers fall back to false, pointer callers fall back to null, and void callers become a no-op when unavailable.
Flag helpers set, clear, assign and test one indexed bit inside the handle flags word; the device-initialized helper ignores null or error handles and otherwise assigns the initialized indicator.
Radix geometry fixes node shift at nine for five-hundred-twelve-byte nodes; fan-out equals node size divided by pointer size and its shift is the binary logarithm of that fan-out.

Maximum depth derives from address width minus node shift divided by fan-out shift, encoded in low bits of the root pointer under a mask. Helpers extract depth, recover the node address, and convert depth to shift and byte-size extents.

Generic tree wrapper holds only a root pointer. Each node is a union of a child-pointer array sized by fan-out for interior use or a byte store sized by node size for leaf use. Type-safe wrappers and initializers build a typed handle around the generic tree with a null root.
Node allocation yields a zero-filled node-sized block for a caller allocation context, and node release returns such a block.

Index translation requires object size to fit within a node, scales directly for power-of-two sizes, and packs other sizes so no object crosses a node boundary by filling each node with a whole count and skipping trailing slack.

Lookup translates an index to a byte offset and descends from the root by level shifts, returning null when beyond current depth or on a missing child. Allocating forms first try the fast lookup then grow the tree, optionally consuming a caller-provided node; additional helpers release the tree or ensure capacity for a count.

Iteration keeps a byte offset plus a logical position. Initialization derives both from a start index; forward and reverse peek return the current object or null at the limit. Advance and rewind update both counters with saturation on overflow and skip node tail slack for non-power sizes. Loop helpers run forward from zero or a start, or backward from the maximum position.
GPIO descriptor collection stores helper array state, a descriptor count, and a trailing flexible array of descriptor pointers.
GPIO flag bit positions place direction-set at bit zero, direction-out at bit one, direction-value at bit two, open-drain at bit three and nonexclusive at bit four.

GPIO initial-state enumeration encodes as-is as zero, input with direction-set alone, low output adding direction-out, high output further adding direction-value, with open-drain variants adding the open-drain bit.

When GPIO consumer support is disabled, acquisition entry points use fixed fallbacks: counting reports zero, mandatory single, indexed and array getters report not-implemented, and optional forms report null, including device-managed variants.

When GPIO support is disabled, release, direction and value helpers warn on any non-null handle, may sleep on release paths, report not-implemented for direction queries, report not single-ended, and report zero for value reads including raw and sleepable array forms.

Flag updates address a single bit via dedicated helpers and tree lookup starts from a single load of the root pointer before descent; fragments show no explicit spinlock, mutex or RCU protection for these paths.
